ops.title: Codex 0.155.1 local plugin MCP launch contract
ops.body:
# Codex 0.155.1 local plugin MCP launch contract

## Verdict

The workable contract for repository-sensitive local MCP servers is a compatibility plugin whose MCP `command` is a bare executable already installed on `PATH`, with no `cwd` field. Codex resolves the executable from `PATH`, starts it in the thread cwd, preserves configured arguments and environment values exactly, and can call its tools.

This is portable across plugin cache versions only when the executable has a separate supported installation path. It is not a self-contained plugin-cache executable. Existing source-built CLIs should therefore expose a stable command and accept explicit Codex/native host arguments; their plugin manifests should invoke that command directly.

No self-contained local stdio packaging shape in Codex CLI 0.155.1 satisfies both requirements:

- Compatibility plugins preserve the thread cwd when `cwd` is omitted, but do not resolve package-relative commands or expand/inject plugin-root variables.
- Portable Agent Plugins resolve package-relative commands and expand/inject `PLUGIN_ROOT` and `PLUGIN_DATA`, but normalize an omitted `cwd` to the installed plugin root.

## Successful runtime proof

The disposable marketplace installed two real plugins into an isolated `CODEX_HOME`. The compatibility plugin declared:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "legacy-bare": {
      "command": "native-probe-mcp",
      "args": ["${PLUGIN_ROOT}", "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}"],
      "env": {
        "PROBE_ENV": "${PLUGIN_ROOT}|${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

The command was present only in `/tmp/codex-port-native-command.EajTzi/bin`, which the isolated app-server process received at the front of `PATH`. The manifest omitted `cwd`.

Run:

```sh
python3 /tmp/codex-port-native-command.EajTzi/probe.py
```

Assertion:

```sh
jq -e '.["call:legacy-bare"].isError == false and .["call:legacy-bare"].structuredContent.cwd == "/private/tmp/codex-port-native-command.EajTzi/workspace"' /tmp/codex-port-native-command.EajTzi/observations.json
```

The assertion returned `true`. `mcpServerStatus/list` reported `legacy-bare` as `connected` with plugin ID `legacy-probe@native-command-probe`, and the direct `mcpServer/tool/call` returned `isError:false`.

The child reported:

- `cwd`: `/private/tmp/codex-port-native-command.EajTzi/workspace`, exactly the thread cwd.
- `script`: `/private/tmp/codex-port-native-command.EajTzi/bin/native-probe-mcp`, proving bare-command `PATH` resolution rather than an absolute manifest argument.
- `argv`: the literal strings `${PLUGIN_ROOT}` and `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}`.
- `PROBE_ENV`: the literal string `${PLUGIN_ROOT}|${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}`.
- `PLUGIN_ROOT`, `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT`, `PLUGIN_DATA`, and `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA`: absent.

## Negative and comparison probes

Three installed compatibility-plugin servers omitted `cwd` and failed startup with `No such file or directory`:

- `./scripts/probe-mcp`
- `${PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/probe-mcp`
- `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/probe-mcp`

The relative command was resolved from the thread cwd, not the installed plugin root. Neither root placeholder was expanded as a compatibility-plugin MCP command.

The installed Agent Plugin used root `plugin.json`, root `mcp.json`, and `command: "./scripts/probe-mcp"`. It connected and answered the same direct tool call. Codex resolved the command to the installed cache copy, expanded `${PLUGIN_ROOT}` and `${PLUGIN_DATA}` in arguments and environment values, and injected both variables.

Its child `cwd` was the installed plugin root, not the thread cwd. `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` and `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA` remained absent. This validates Agent Plugin packaging but rejects it for repository-sensitive local MCP servers under the stated cwd invariant.

## Source and documentation evidence

The installed binary is `codex-cli 0.155.1`. The matching upstream tag `rust-v0.155.1` resolves to commit `be2951ea34f0d295ed0becf97079f92fa5f6950e` in the disposable source clone.

At that revision:

- `codex-rs/utils/plugins/src/plugin_namespace.rs:42-79#fayt` selects a recognized root Agent Plugin manifest before compatibility manifests.
- `codex-rs/codex-mcp/src/agent_plugin_config.rs:145-235#tj58` resolves contained `./` commands beneath the plugin root, expands `PLUGIN_ROOT` and `PLUGIN_DATA` in arguments and environment values, defaults omitted `cwd` to `${PLUGIN_ROOT}`, and injects those two variables.
- `codex-rs/codex-mcp/src/plugin_config.rs:65-145#r125` sends host compatibility-plugin MCP objects through regular MCP deserialization without Agent Plugin normalization.
- `codex-rs/rmcp-client/src/stdio_server_launcher.rs:260-292#xhrj` uses the thread launcher fallback cwd when configuration omits `cwd`, then resolves the program against that cwd and the constructed environment.

The official packaging guide distinguishes portable root `plugin.json` plus `mcp.json` from the `.codex-plugin/plugin.json` plus `.mcp.json` compatibility layout. It documents `PLUGIN_ROOT`, `PLUGIN_DATA`, `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT`, and `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA` for plugin hooks, not compatibility-plugin MCP children: <https://developers.openai.com/plugins/build/plugins>.

## Current runtime inventory

Observed on 2026-09-23 without restarting processes:

- Homebrew CLI: `/opt/homebrew/Caskroom/codex/0.155.1/bin/codex`, `codex-cli 0.155.1`, SHA-256 `8eaf1ad12fe6bf89b1710330f58900014322c7c5af677e43be116d8ac5fc0a9e`.
- Active shared app-server: PID `42272`, started 2026-09-21 22:08:40 local time, with its loaded text image at the same 0.155.1 path.
- Codex desktop bundle: `26.915.31945` build `9922`; bundled runtime `/Applications/Codex.app/Contents/Resources/codex` reports `codex-cli 0.155.0-alpha.9.2`, SHA-256 `9280c0754e8f1f6b72f495d30c8c82a006dbc4995bf0492916fa0901f6bfd1f9`.
- Orca application bundle and active main process: `1.4.209`.

## Limits

- The proof made no model request and started no model turn.
- All plugin installation, configuration, cache, source clone, and executable writes were under `/tmp/codex-port-native-command.EajTzi`.
- No repository source, user configuration, global plugin cache, live application, or existing app-server process was changed or restarted.
- The bare-command result proves the contract for a separately installed executable on `PATH`; it does not make a script stored only in the plugin cache discoverable.
- Agent Plugin mode remains appropriate where plugin-root cwd is acceptable or where the MCP server is remote. It is not acceptable for the existing repository-identity contract.
